newsitem.title: USA: Most IMM currencies close higher, Swiss paces gain.
newsitem.headline: Most IMM currencies close higher, Swiss paces gain.

text.p: IMM currency futures finished mostly higher, with Swiss francs leading the march upward after midday, floor traders said.

Market participants linked the gains in Swiss francs to activity in the mark/Swiss cross reflecting current thinking that broad inclusion in European monetary union portends a soft single currency and soft mark.
"Swiss has been a haven currency while EMU continues to erupt," said an IMM floor analyst.

Some investors were thought to be unwinding previously established positions in the spread, liquidating marks and buying Swiss. Buy stops were triggered above $0.6900 in September Swiss francs, accelerating the move.

September marks set a contract low for the second straight session in morning pit trade, falling to $0.5690 before bouncing back to end the day around unchanged. Spot dollar/mark softened in the afternoon after climbing earlier to a new 41-month of 1.7650.
Yen futures also recovered from an earlier dip to end near steady after largely ignoring overnight current account data.
The sharp rise in Japan's May current account surplus, which soared 154.9 percent from a year earlier, had been widely expected.
British pound futures ended lower in a technical setback following Tuesday's rally to a six-month high of $1.6910, floor traders said.

The market is focused on the conclusion of the Bank of England's policy committee meeting Thursday and has built in expectations for a British interest rate hike of at least 25 basis points and possibly 50, traders said.
Some floor traders predicted the anticipated announcement of higher rates would touch off a rally in pound futures followed by a profit-taking selloff.
"That should be viewed as a buying opportunity for further strength in the pound," one brokerage trader said.
Traders and analysts also predicted more gains ahead for the dollar at the expense of a lower-drifting mark.

However, they said futures could range-trade heading into Friday's U.S. producer price index data for June. Economists on average look for an unchanged overall index, with the core index excluding food and energy prices rising 0.1 percent.

September yen ended unchanged at $0.008953, marks unchanged at $0.5708, Swiss francs up $0.0037 at $0.6916, sterling down $0.0034 at $1.6820, Canadian dollars up $0.0002 at $0.7306, Australian dollars down $0.0019 at $0.7453 and Mexican pesos up $0.000250 at $0.123525. ((Chicago Derivatives desk 312-408-8750))
